summary: Verified the Sep 12 2026 by-product retry-skip data-integrity fix (real incident Lot 72722). Backend: wrote and ran 9 pytest unit cases against production_confirmation_service.find_successful_byproduct_confirmation + log_confirmation - all 9 PASSED. Covered every branch called out in the review request: (a) returns byproduct_confirmation dict when latest history for lot+RP has main success=False AND byproduct success=True AND matching byproduct_material_output_uuid, (b) returns None for a DIFFERENT byproduct_material_output_uuid, (c) returns None for a different reporting_point_id, (d) returns None once a newer history record shows the main confirmation finally succeeded, (e) returns None when no history, (f) returns None when the by-product itself did not succeed, (g) new_byproduct_product_id matching path (reuse on match, None on mismatch), (h) only looks at the LATEST record (older successful attempts don't hide a newer main-failed one), (i) log_confirmation now persists new_byproduct_product_id so a later retry can identify the same target. Code review of server.py _confirm_production_inner (lines 2843-2895): confirmed the new find_successful_byproduct_confirmation call runs FIRST, and the if/elif/elif chain has exactly the 3 branches described (reuse when returned dict is not None; else confirm_material_output for existing byproduct_material_output_uuid; else create_material_output for a brand-new by-product line). Short-circuit is genuine (elif not else if). Frontend: on /production-confirmation > Production Confirmation tab, verified via UI + code review that the WIP filter now applies EITHER (wip exists && !skipped && !success) OR (conf.success===false) - see visibleRows useMemo lines 2275-2289. WIP:Posted still ONLY matches (wip && !wip.skipped && wip.success) - unchanged. UI screenshot confirms WIP:Error selection + Clear Filters button behavior. Dev env has 0 open lots for the super_admin session ("No rows match 'Show mine' - no open lots were created by you."), so a positive live-data-driven Posted vs Error row-count assertion was not possible - explicitly flagged as code-review-only for that data path, per the request's own note that this is acceptable when live SAP failure isn't reproducible.
critical_code_review_comments: ProductionConfirmationPage.js is now 2650 lines - still well past the 700-line guideline (called out in iter_160 and iter_161 too, no action yet).

find_successful_byproduct_confirmation only guards against re-posting when the LATEST history record is the failed one. If a user retries and the retry ALSO fails to post the main output but for some reason writes a new history row that itself already includes a re-computed byproduct_confirmation.success=True (which _confirm_production_inner does after reuse: log_confirmation always writes result[byproduct_confirmation] into the row), the next retry after that will still correctly find the LATEST row and skip - behavior is safe. Verified by test_only_considers_latest_record.

Consider adding an idempotency key stored on the history record so cross-server retries with the same request UUID short-circuit even before this lookup. Currently the safety net is 'latest record for (lot, RP)' which works because there's a single serialized retry flow via job_store, but if multiple concurrent retries were ever allowed the race could still double-post. Out of scope for this fix.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of code-testable paths (env has 0 open SAP lots so live-data Posted/Error row counting was code-review verified)

seed_data_creation: Only ephemeral test data (TESTLOT_ITER162_A, TESTLOT_ITER162_B in production_confirmation_history) - inserted and deleted within each pytest run, nothing left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 162 verified the by-product retry-skip fix at the unit level (9 passing tests) and the WIP:Error broadened-filter at the code+UI-rendering level. End-to-end live SAP retry was NOT reproducible (this dev tenant has 0 open SAP lots for the test super_admin) - the main agent stated this in the request as an acceptable limitation. If a future iteration ever hits a real failing-main-confirmation lot in this tenant, positively assert that (i) it appears under WIP:Error, and (ii) a real second confirm submission for that lot does NOT re-issue confirm_material_output/create_material_output (check backend logs for the two SAP method names).
rca of the issue: Original prod bug (Lot 72722): SAP's confirm_material_output/create_material_output are ADD operations - each call increments the running scrap total, never overwrites. The old flow posted by-product BEFORE main, so a main-confirmation failure led users to retry, and every retry re-posted the same scrap qty. Fix: production_confirmation_service.find_successful_byproduct_confirmation looks at the LATEST history row for the exact (production_lot_id, reporting_point_id) tuple - if main failed but by-product succeeded AND the retry targets the same by-product identity (existing MaterialOutput UUID OR same new_byproduct_product_id for the create path), the retry reuses the earlier byproduct_confirmation dict and skips the SAP call entirely. Once main finally succeeds, the newest history row has success=True and this lookup returns None again so subsequent unrelated confirmations aren't wrongly short-circuited. WIP:Error frontend broadening (visibleRows useMemo) was independent: previously (wip && !skipped && !success) only, which never fires when the MAIN confirm fails because wip_clearing stays null - now also OR'd with (conf.success === false) so a stuck main-failed lot is visible.
